capture.final_message:
Use the representation of `DoubleCoset.Quotient H K` as the quotient of `G` by the double-coset setoid.

Establish three basic quotient facts:

1. The setoid relation satisfies  
   \(x \sim y \iff \exists h\in H,\ \exists k\in K,\ y=(hx)k\).

2. An element \(a\) belongs to the double coset represented by \(i\) exactly when  
   `DoubleCoset.mk H K a = i`.

3. Every quotient is represented by its chosen representative:  
   `DoubleCoset.mk H K (Quotient.out q) = q`.

The two sides of the first displayed `Iff` then hold independently by (1) and (2), so their equivalence is immediate.

For the finiteness equivalence, if the quotient is finite, take the finset of all quotient classes; (2) shows their associated double cosets cover `G`. Conversely, from a finite family `I` covering `G`, apply the cover to `Quotient.out q` for an arbitrary quotient class `q`. Facts (2) and (3) show that `q` equals some member of `I`. Thus every quotient class lies in a fixed finite set, proving the quotient finite. The remaining side of the second `Iff` is exactly fact (3), so again both propositions are true independently.
